subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspace confinement a default hard boundary, keep it as opt-in sandbox/tool policy, or split this into narrower filesystem, exec, and skill-workspace fixes?
rationale: The remaining work changes a security boundary and can break existing trusted host-wide workflows, while current open PRs address only subsets of the requested isolation.

options.title: Define default confinement and migration
options.body: Choose the default workspace/file-tool posture, preserve intentional host-wide workflows through explicit opt-out or migration guidance, and require tests/docs for file tools plus exec/sandbox scope.

options.title: Keep isolation opt-in
options.body: Leave current defaults as documented and use this issue to improve docs, Doctor guidance, and setup prompts for users who need `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` or sandboxing.

options.title: Split and close after narrower owners exist
options.body: Move path ACLs, exec isolation, local-user sandboxing, and skill workspace routing into canonical linked items, then close this only after the concrete report has no unique remaining work.

recommendation.title: Define default confinement and migration
recommendation.body: Choose the default workspace/file-tool posture, preserve intentional host-wide workflows through explicit opt-out or migration guidance, and require tests/docs for file tools plus exec/sandbox scope.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest prior review and filesystem-policy routing signal for this security-boundary decision.
